chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
One who fulfils the need of a Muslim will be called out to by Allah (Exalted and Mighty) saying, 'your reward is upon Me, and I shall not be satisfied with a reward for you less than Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fulfilling the needs of a Muslim according to Imam al-Baqir (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (a.s.) highlights the immense spiritual weight of relieving a believer's distress, framing it as a direct divine guarantee. The phrase 'thawabuka 'alayya' (your reward is upon Me) signifies that Allah assumes full responsibility for the recompense, ensuring that Paradise is the minimum threshold for such an act of kindness.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 118. It has been reported that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said:
One who fulfils the need of a Muslim will be called out to by Allah [M.G] saying, 'your reward is upon Me and I shall not be satisfied with a reward for you less than Paradise.
